body:
Fixes #136

C# CI no longer requires `CODECOV_TOKEN`, and Rust PR checks now catch the production compilation error that stopped Auto Release. npm publishing uses its verified OIDC policy without a long-lived token fallback.

- Remove the Codecov token gate; upload with `codecov-action@v7`, `use_oidc: true`, and `id-token: write`. Retain Cobertura reports as an artifact and write coverage totals to the Actions summary before contacting Codecov. Only a confirmed unactivated/missing repository permits upload failure, with an explicit warning. Activated repositories and unexpected API failures remain strict.
- Move the test-only `PathBuf` import into the tests module. Build all 16 executable Rust helpers in their non-test release configuration with `-D warnings` on PRs. Add the standalone path helper's missing dependency declaration and a patch release fragment.
- Add isolated, authentication-only dispatch modes for crates.io, NuGet, and npm. npm's live OIDC exchange succeeded, so its token fallback is removed. Validate already-published npm versions with `npm pack --dry-run`; retain publish dry runs for new versions.

### Reproduction and verification

Before the fix, building the `version-and-commit.rs` manifest generated by `rust-script --package` with `RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo build --release --manifest-path ...` failed on the unused `PathBuf`. The new PR compilation check passes for every executable helper. The existing throwaway-repository release experiment also completed versioning, changelog collection, commit, tag, and push to its local bare origin with warnings denied.

Regression tests cover Codecov activation/error handling, real Cobertura summary generation, compilation command flags and failure propagation, OIDC token exchange, and both published/unpublished npm dry-run paths. The npm regression failed before its fix, matching CI's `You cannot publish over the previously published versions: 0.1.0` error.

Local validation: 553 C# tests; 370 Rust tests (two existing ignores); 29 release-helper tests; 217 JavaScript/workflow tests; 37 client tests and type declarations; seven WebAssembly tests; the browser app production build; Node/Bun/Deno conformance (32 passed, four expected skips per runtime); all 16 production helper builds; formatting, both Clippy workspaces, actionlint/ShellCheck, and zizmor. The cross-backend synthetic check returned identical data from Rust, C#, and WebAssembly. [C# CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40094288203) successfully uploaded coverage using OIDC without an upload secret, and [Rust CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40094288283) passed the production helper builds and OS matrix. [npm authentication verification](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40094153480) passed without publishing.

### Blocked acceptance criteria — unfinished

- **crates.io:** the latest [live authentication job](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095765020/job/120877585051) returned HTTP 400: `No Trusted Publishing config found for repository link-foundation/link-cli`. A [read-only configuration probe](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095765020/job/120877585206) using the existing publishing token received HTTP 403: `this token does not have the required permissions to perform this action`. The probe was removed after collecting evidence; it did not change configuration or disclose credentials. A crate owner with account access or an appropriately scoped token must configure `rust.yml` as a trusted publisher. The release secret fallbacks remain until authentication is verified, as required by the issue.
- **NuGet:** the [live authentication job](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40094151877) returned HTTP 401: `No matching trust policy owned by user 'konard' was found`. There is no configured `NUGET_USER`; the policy creator's personal account must be identified/configured and verified for both packages before removing the API-key fallbacks. This result applies to the tested account, not every possible NuGet account.
- A green **main** run and the next real Rust Auto Release require a post-merge run and registry publication. PR checks and an isolated local release do not establish those final acceptance criteria. Keep this PR unmerged while the registry requirements remain blocked.

The existing crates.io token lacks permission to administer trust. NuGet policy creation requires an authenticated account session; the publishing API key does not provide one. The available GitHub credential cannot configure the external registry accounts. [Requirement mapping, diagnostic commands, exact evidence, and remaining setup](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-136-fb310c545174/docs/case-studies/issue-136/README.md) are recorded in the repository.

### Final PR checks

All eight workflows passed at final head `e13051a5dd63d3cb62aa27c78f94762eb358cca5` (runs created 2026-10-24 12:54:32 UTC, after the commit): [C#](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095878362), [Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095878401), [JS client](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095878501), [WebAssembly](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095878369), [workflow lint and regression tests](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095878474), [security](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095878483), [dependencies](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095878395), and [links](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/40095878358). These results cover the PR; the external and post-merge criteria above remain unfinished. The branch contains the latest `main`, and the working tree is clean.

<details>
<summary>Preserved investigation logs and exact error locations</summary>

Full downloaded logs are retained in the workspace under `experiments/issue-136/ci-logs/`:

| Log | Line | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `csharp-40087795597.log` | 738 | Mandatory upload-token gate fails main. |
| `rust-40087795520.log` | 5511 | Non-test release compilation rejects the unused `PathBuf` import. |
| `js-client-40094288228.log` | 1499 | Publish dry run rejects the existing npm version. |
| `trust-crates-job.log` | 45 | Registry rejects OIDC: no matching trusted publishing configuration. |
| `trust-crates-latest-job.log` | 45 | The isolated final authentication diagnostic confirms the configuration is still absent. |
| `registry-admin-access.log` | 57–58 | The existing publishing token receives HTTP 403 when reading trusted publisher settings. |
| `trust-nuget-job.log` | 60 | Registry rejects OIDC: no matching policy for `konard`. |
| `csharp-oidc-coverage.log` | 1462, 1481, 1828 | Coverage artifact retained, strict upload enabled, OIDC upload queued successfully. |
| `final-csharp-40095878362.log` | 5343–5344, 5376, 5392–5395, 5740 | Final head: coverage totals, artifact retained, strict OIDC upload queued successfully. |

The linked workflow runs preserve the corresponding remote evidence. The initial Rust and NuGet diagnostic workflows were cancelled after their failed authentication jobs completed; the job logs establish those registry failures. The latest isolated Rust diagnostic completed with failure and confirmed both the absent trust configuration and insufficient configuration permissions.

</details>
title: Use OIDC for coverage and npm; compile Rust release helpers before merge
